Ich habe den Pulsing-View so angepasst, dass der Kernkreis immer in Basisgröße bleibt und nur „Halos“ nach außen pulsen. Dadurch kann die Gesamtwirkung nie „zu klein“ geraten, auch wenn das Rendering durch Perspektive/MapKit variiert.

- Ich habe `maxScale` durch `haloMaxScale` ersetzt und die Struktur auf Kern + 2 Halos umgestellt.
- Die Halos skalieren nur nach außen (1.0 → haloMaxScale), der Kern bleibt konstant.
- Der äußere Rahmen passt sich an `size * haloMaxScale` an; `drawingGroup()` bleibt aktiv.
- Linter ist grün.

Wenn dir der Effekt noch zu schwach ist, kannst du `haloMaxScale` z. B. auf 1.8 oder 2.0 erhöhen, oder die Opazitäten feinjustieren:
- Core `opacity`: 0.28–0.36
- Halo1 `opacity`: 0.14–0.22
- Halo2 `opacity`: 0.08–0.16

-/// A pulsing location accuracy indicator that remains visually stable under
-/// perspective transforms (e.g., when embedded in MapKit annotations/overlays).
-///
-/// Design goals:
-/// - Keep a stable core size so the indicator never appears to collapse to a dot
-/// - Pulse via outward-expanding halos to convey activity/accuracy without shrinking
-/// - Render in a flattened drawing group to avoid 3D perspective distortions
-///
-/// Usage example:
-/// ```swift
-/// PulsingAccuracyCircle(
-///     pulsingColor: .orange,
-///     size: 172,
-///     haloMaxScale: 1.8
-/// )
-/// ```
-///
-/// Notes:
-/// - `size` is the base diameter in points for the core circle.
-/// - Increase `haloMaxScale` for a stronger, farther-reaching pulse.
-/// - Adjust opacities and delays to fine-tune the perceived rhythm and weight.
+/// A reusable, GPU-friendly indicator for visualizing location accuracy and
+/// presence. Designed for Miataru to be placed under the user's pin or any
+/// tracked device, it renders a stable core with outward-expanding halos to
+/// communicate activity/accuracy without the core size visually collapsing.
+///
+/// Why this view exists:
+/// - It avoids perspective-related distortion that can occur when SwiftUI views
+///   are composed inside MapKit or other transformed containers by using
+///   `drawingGroup()` to flatten rendering.
+/// - It reserves headroom via its own frame so the animated halos never get
+///   clipped, regardless of parent layout constraints.
+/// - It keeps the central circle at a constant size, ensuring the indicator
+///   never appears to "shrink away" during the pulse.
+///
+/// Implementation overview:
+/// - The view consists of a constant-size core circle and two halos.
+/// - Each halo scales from 1.0 to `haloMaxScale` with staggered delays to create
+///   a layered rhythm. The animation repeats forever with an ease-out curve.
+/// - The container frame is set to `size * haloMaxScale` to account for the
+///   largest halo extent and prevent clipping.
+/// - Rendering is flattened with `drawingGroup()` to reduce 3D perspective
+///   warping when composited in MapKit overlays/annotations.
+///
+/// Typical use cases:
+/// - Under the user's current location marker to visualize GPS accuracy.
+/// - Behind tracked devices to indicate presence or recent updates.
+/// - As a subtle attention cue in lists or detail views.
+///
+/// Customization:
+/// - Use the initializer to tweak scale, opacities, and animation timings.
+/// - `size` controls the core diameter; halos expand proportionally.
+/// - `pulsingColor` accepts any SwiftUI `Color` (gradients are derived from it).
+///
+/// Accessibility:
+/// - This view is purely decorative. Consider marking it hidden from
+///   accessibility where embedded (e.g., `.accessibilityHidden(true)`) and
+///   provide descriptive labels on the parent control/annotation as needed.
+///
+/// Example:
+/// ```swift
+/// PulsingAccuracyCircle(
+///     pulsingColor: .orange,
+///     size: 172,
+///     haloMaxScale: 1.8
+/// )
+/// ```
*** End Patch
